name: ANI-II 00 — Identified line, no special treatment

technical_body.meaning: Identified line — no special treatment
technical_body.notes: Ordinary POTS residence or single-line business. The 'null' info-digit prefix; anything that is not one of the special classes below defaults to 00.

technical_body.meaning: Multiparty line — Operator Number Identification required
technical_body.notes: The originating switch cannot uniquely identify which subscriber on the multiparty (2-, 4-, 8-party) line placed the call. An operator must intercept and key-pulse the calling number. Effectively retired with the last multiparty loops (rural, ~2005).

technical_body.meaning: ANI failure — originating switch could not deliver a calling number
technical_body.notes: A soft failure code the far end interprets as 'no calling number available'. Historic reasons: switch software fault, translation table miss, tandem hop that stripped ANI. On SS7 today, delivered as OLI 02 alongside a CgPN parameter that may or may not be present.

name: ANI-II 06 — Hotel/motel guest station without CDR

technical_body.meaning: Hotel/motel guest station without call-detail recording — station follows the hotel PBX billing
technical_body.notes: Distinguishes a room extension from the hotel's main published DID. Terminating carrier uses this to route to a hotel-billing pipeline instead of the calling party's LEC bill.

technical_body.meaning: Special operator handling required
technical_body.notes: Flags calls that must be intercepted by an operator regardless of routing — e.g., certain restricted-CoS station types.

technical_body.meaning: Test call from a network test facility
technical_body.notes: Sent by CO/tandem test lines and cross-connect test panels. Terminating switch treats as maintenance traffic (does not bill, may skip announcement replacements).

technical_body.meaning: AIOD — listed DN from a PBX with Automatic Identified Outward Dialing
technical_body.notes: The PBX sends the specific station's number as ANI instead of the trunk group's billing number, so long-distance calls can be billed per extension. Common on old Centrex.

technical_body.meaning: Coin or coinless payphone (historic combined class)
technical_body.notes: Original combined class. Split circa 1988: coin-supervised ACTS phones -> 27; coinless private paystations -> 70.

disputed.split_effective_date: The 23 -> 27/70 split is documented as a late-1980s NANPA action; exact effective date varied by LEC. Some independents kept using 23 into the early 1990s.

technical_body.meaning: Inbound to an 800/toll-free number
technical_body.notes: Marks the leg as toll-free-terminated so the RESPORG's IXC pays and the calling party isn't charged. Sent alongside the actual ANI so the 8YY subscriber can screen or route by origin.

technical_body.meaning: Inbound to a 900 premium number
technical_body.notes: Marks the leg as premium-billed so the LEC applies the per-minute charge to the calling party's bill on behalf of the 900 information provider.

technical_body.meaning: Coin payphone — ACTS-equipped, coin-supervised
technical_body.notes: Post-1988 split from 23. Downstream carriers use it to enforce coin-call restrictions and coin-return semantics. Not delivered by locally-validating COCOTs on residential POTS (those look like 00).

technical_body.meaning: Call originated from an ITS (Inmate Telephone System)
technical_body.notes: Signals that the calling party is an incarcerated person on a facility-restricted line. Terminating carriers use it to block collect-refusal loopholes and to enforce facility screening.

technical_body.meaning: Intercept — call reached a blank/non-working number

name: ANI-II 31 — Intercept: trouble (line out of service)

technical_body.meaning: Intercept — trouble condition
Intercept — regular (referral or changed-number treatment)
Call already handled by a telco operator (assistance operator)
technical_body.notes: Prevents double-operator loops on collect and third-party billed calls.

technical_body.meaning: Outward Wide-Area Telephone Service — bulk-billed outbound
technical_body.notes: OUTWATS trunks let large customers make unlimited outbound calls in a defined band for a flat rate. Largely retired as long-distance minutes commoditized in the late 1990s.

technical_body.meaning: TRS — unrestricted origin (Title IV ADA relay service)
technical_body.notes: Assigned in the wake of the ADA (effective July 26, 1993). Signals that the call is being placed via a TRS operator for a deaf/HoH caller.

technical_body.meaning: Cellular / wireless PCS — Type 1 interconnection (wireline-format ANI, no ESRD)
technical_body.notes: Wireless carrier connects to the wireline network like a Class-5 subscriber; ANI is the caller's MDN in wireline format. Historically the majority of AMPS/TDMA cellular traffic delivered to landline destinations.

technical_body.meaning: Cellular / wireless PCS — Type 2 interconnection (roamer default)
Cellular / wireless PCS — Type 2 (roamer, alternate)
TRS call originating from a hotel/motel guest line
TRS call originating from a restricted line (prison/inmate + TRS)
Line connected to a private paystation (coinless payphone; charge-a-call, hospital, hotel-lobby, coinless inmate)
technical_body.notes: The post-1988 split-mate of code 27. Signals a customer-owned coinless phone that bills the coinless service subscriber rather than the caller-per-call.

name: ANI-II 93 — Access for private virtual network (VPN)

technical_body.meaning: Access for private virtual network (VPN, off-net access) — enterprise trunk
technical_body.notes: Marks calls that entered the public network from an enterprise VPN. Distinguished from AIOD (20) — AIOD is per-station billing on a listed Centrex; 93 is a VPN trunk carrying multiple sites.

technical_body.meaning: Reserved for future assignment (per era)
technical_body.notes: Reserved on a period-1998-authoritative NANPA letter. Some entries (78 for VoIP originations; 21/22 for AIOD-related sub-classes; certain 08 historical 'InterLATA restricted' notes) have been reassigned or proposed on later letters. A record for the era's ANI-II set should query BY YEAR — a 2026 answer may differ from a 1998 answer.

disputed.later_assignments: Post-2003 NANPA letters have reassigned some of the previously-reserved codes (notably 78 in some carrier profiles for VoIP originations). Always cite the letter version by date when returning a value.

technical_body.meaning: How the 2-digit info-digit prefix reaches the terminating switch
technical_body.delivery_mf: On Feature Group D MF trunks, delivered inband as KP + II + KP + ANI + ST — the FIRST KP is the info-digit start, II is the 2-digit prefix, the second KP delimits from the calling-number spill, ANI is 10 digits, ST terminates.
technical_body.delivery_ss7: On SS7 ISUP, delivered as the OLI (Originating Line Information) parameter — 1 octet, hex 00-63, mapping to decimal 00-99.
technical_body.notes: Early PC-based scanners like 'ANI II Sniffer' (~1995) sat on 800 terminations and logged the II byte for every inbound call. This is how phreaks catalogued which lines were payphones vs. hotels vs. cellular in the wild.
